expectations.text: Clearly recommends splitting the file (does NOT advise keeping it as one file)
expectations.evidence: Title 'Split it — but along the seams that already exist'; 'Split it by concern, keep each resulting file cohesive and self-contained, and stop there.'

expectations.text: Justifies the split by multiple independent concerns AND/OR exceeding the ~300-line ceiling, not blind line count
expectations.evidence: 'It's five unrelated concerns sharing a filename by accident'; 'at ~550 lines you're well past the point where signal-to-noise starts hurting an agent'; explicitly warns against reflex-splitting on line count.

expectations.text: Notes each group (dates/currency/validation/etc.) can be understood in isolation, so the boundaries are clean
expectations.evidence: 'Each of these passes the test that matters: can it be understood in isolation? Yes — every group is self-contained, mostly pure functions, props/args in and values out.'

expectations.text: Corrects the misapplied 'big files are fine for agents' reasoning (that defense is for one cohesive concern, not a grab-bag)
expectations.evidence: 'that argument only applies to code that's cohesive'; 'Bigger files win when the contents are one thing... They lose when the file is a junk drawer of unrelated things.'
